strategy.observation: Linear says it powers more than 40,000 product teams, so your customer base likely includes a large pool of the exact people product teams interview when validating workflows and buying decisions.
strategy.offer_link: If your team needs to talk to current product-team users, a service that recruits and schedules interview participants could reduce the time spent finding the right matches and coordinating sessions.
hypotheses: I’m assuming your product organization runs regular customer interviews to inform roadmap decisions.
I’m assuming it can still take meaningful effort to identify and schedule the right customers, even with a large user base.
I’m assuming you would value outside help only if it saves your team time without lowering participant quality.
strategy.angle: Linear already has a built-in audience of 40,000+ product teams, which could make customer interview recruiting much easier if your team needs it.
strategy.fit_reason: The fit is plausible because Linear’s customers are exactly the kind of product users a product team would interview, and the scale of that base suggests enough potential participants. But there’s no fact showing a current research bottleneck or active hiring/research push, so the case for outsourcing recruiting is still a stretch.

draft.subject: Interview recruiting for Linear
draft.body:
Hi,

Linear’s 40,000+ product teams look like a strong pool for customer interviews.

I help product teams recruit and schedule the right participants for interviews. If your team runs regular discovery or roadmap conversations, my guess is the time sink is still finding the right users and getting them on the calendar.

Do you already have a standard process for turning that user base into interview participants, or is it still handled case by case?
